name: Quote and process early buyouts
summary: A customer or a dealer asks what it would cost to end a lease early, usually to buy the equipment, refinance it or trade it up for new equipment. Customer service gives standard quotes straight from the lease system; non-standard contracts go to a lease administration specialist, sometimes with a valuation from asset management and a manager's approval. About four in ten quotes are paid; then cash application finds the funds, the specialist matches and posts the payoff, refunds any debit taken in the meantime, tells treasury if the contract sat in a securitised pool and asks the title team to discharge the registration. Most elapsed time is the customer deciding, queues between teams and unidentified incoming funds; errors come from expired quotes, debits in flight and missed assets.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active small and mid-ticket contracts, a commercial lease management system, contracts funded partly through bank-sponsored securitisation conduits and a lease administration team of about 11.
baseline.notes: Payout quotes for simple $1 or fixed-option contracts come from customer service; complex ones from lease administration. Funds arrive by wire, EFT, cheque or dealer cheque.

trigger: A customer calls or emails customer service, or a dealer asks its account manager, for an early payout figure on an active contract.
end_state: The quote expires unused, or the payout is received, the contract is terminated, refunds are issued, treasury and the title team are notified and the entries are posted.

volume.seasonality: Somewhat higher in spring and at calendar year end when dealers push trade-ups; payout requests fell in spring 2020 while deferral requests rose.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map: about 1.5% of 55,000 active contracts ask for a quote each month. About 320 completed payouts a month fits the file's statement that about 30% of booked contracts end early.

Title, department, layer and loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). NBC shows customer service giving buyout quotes. FTE is the author's estimate from step times: about 20 minutes per request on intake, routing and standard quotes, about a tenth of the customer service team.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)
Document imaging and contract file store
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Online auction and equipment listing platforms
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)

steps.name: Take payout request and verify the requester
steps.description: A customer service representative answers the call or opens the email or portal message, finds the contract in the lease system and confirms the caller is an authorised signer or guarantor by checking name, address and recent payment details. The representative records what is wanted: full payout, payout of one asset, a trade-up, and the date the customer intends to pay.
inputs: payout request (call, email or portal message)

error.defect_description: Wrong contract or schedule picked when the customer has several schedules.

control.basis: Caller authentication policy protecting owner and guarantor personal information (PIPEDA safeguards principle)

next.condition: request from a dealer for a trade-up

evidence.note: Customer service as the entry point for buyout quotes and dealers as requesters are documented; the 32% dealer share and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm dealer trade-up and customer authorisation
steps.description: The dealer usually calls its vendor account manager because it needs the payout figure to write a new lease for replacement equipment. The account manager checks the new deal's status in the origination portal, confirms the customer has signed an authorisation letting the dealer receive account information, and emails lease administration asking for a quick quote.

error.defect_description: Payout figure released to the dealer without the customer's authorisation.

control.basis: Customer consent before disclosing account information to a third party (PIPEDA consent principle and company privacy policy)

evidence.note: Dealer buyout quote requests and trade-up figures are documented; the consent check, minutes and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer signs authorisation for the dealer
steps.description: The dealer or account manager sends the customer a one-page authorisation to release the payout figure and waits for it to come back signed by email or e-signature. Small business owners often take a day or more to return it while they decide on the new equipment.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate of a common privacy safeguard in dealer-requested quotes.

steps.name: Check whether the contract qualifies for a standard quote
steps.description: The representative opens the contract summary in the lease system and checks the flags that decide who prepares the quote: one schedule, a fixed purchase option such as $1 or a stated percentage, payments current, no collections or legal status, not a mid-ticket or fair market value contract and not a partial payout.

error.defect_description: A non-standard contract is treated as standard, for example a second schedule or pending insurance charge is missed.

evidence.note: Split of standard and non-standard quotes is an author estimate for a small-ticket portfolio.

steps.name: Generate a standard payout quote and send it
steps.description: For a standard contract the representative runs the payout quote function in the lease system, which adds the remaining payments (discounted where the contract says so), the purchase option, arrears and fees, and sales tax for the province, less any deposit. The representative checks the good-until date falls before the next billing date where possible, emails the quote letter with payment instructions and notes the contract.

error.defect_description: Wrong tax province or a good-until date that crosses a billing date, so the payment received falls short.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreements: a full prepayment may be accepted only at not less than the contract's prepayment amount

evidence.note: Quote components and the prepayment floor in securitised pools are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Route the request to the lease administration queue
steps.description: For a non-standard contract the representative creates a work item in the lease system service queue and types in the requester, contact details, quote date wanted, trade-up flag and any authorisation, copying details from the call notes or email.

error.defect_description: Missing quote date or contact detail, so the specialist has to call back.

evidence.note: Re-keying from call notes into the queue is an author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Review contract terms and account status
steps.description: A lease administration specialist opens the signed contract in the imaging system to read the early termination clause, purchase option and discount rate, then checks the lease system for arrears, debits already sent to the bank, late fees, protection program charges, multiple assets and whether the contract sits in a securitised pool.

error.defect_description: Contract clause misread, for example a fair market value option treated as a fixed option.

next.condition: fair market value or mid-ticket asset

evidence.note: The inputs a payoff quote needs are documented; queue time and the share needing a valuation are author estimates.

steps.name: Provide fair market value or residual for the quote
steps.description: An asset manager values the equipment for contracts with a fair market value option or a large residual, using recent auction results, listing sites, residual tables and sometimes condition details from the dealer, and records the value and its basis on the work item.

error.defect_description: Stale or optimistic value that later produces a remarketing loss or customer pushback.

evidence.note: Manual fair market value entry for residual-based payoffs is documented; minutes and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Calculate the payout in the lease system
steps.description: The specialist runs the payoff quote function: chooses the method the contract requires (present value of remaining payments at the contract rate, or remaining payments in full), sets the effective date, adds the purchase option or valuation, arrears, fees and sales tax by province, deducts the deposit, and for a one-asset payout splits the schedule. The quote is saved for later payoff processing.

error.defect_description: Wrong effective date, a missed asset or a wrong tax rate.

evidence.note: Calculation steps follow lease system documentation and the prepayment amount definition; minutes and the approval share are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve a non-standard or high-value quote
steps.description: The lease administration manager reviews quotes that depart from the contract formula: discounts a dealer asked for on a trade-up, waived fees, residual write-downs, amounts above the specialist's limit or a figure below the prepayment amount on a securitised contract. The manager approves, changes or rejects it in the work item.

error.defect_description: Concession approved without checking the pool status.

control.basis: Delegated authority matrix for payout concessions and fee waivers

evidence.note: Approval thresholds and shares are author estimates of a common delegated authority design.

steps.name: Issue the payout quote letter
steps.description: The specialist generates the quote letter from the lease system template with the good-until date, daily interest after that date, payment instructions and a note that scheduled debits continue until the payout is received, then emails it to the customer and, when authorised, the dealer, and notes the contract.

error.defect_description: Quote sent to the wrong contact.

evidence.note: Good Until date on saved quotes is documented; letter content and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer or dealer decides and arranges funds
steps.description: The customer compares the payout with keeping the lease, arranges a bank loan or the dealer's new lease, or does nothing. Many quotes are requested for budgeting, refinancing comparisons or trade-ins that do not happen, and simply expire.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: funds sent within the quote period
quote expired or new date wanted, requote

evidence.note: About 40% of quotes convert, as in the organisation file's process note; the requote share and decision times are author estimates.

steps.name: Identify and apply payout funds
steps.description: A cash application clerk finds the wire, EFT or cheque in the bank portal or lockbox file, often with no contract number or a dealer's reference, matches it to the contract from the quote list or by calling the payer, posts it to suspense on the contract in the lease system and emails lease administration.

error.defect_description: Funds applied to the wrong contract or left unidentified.

evidence.note: Suspense balances in payoff processing are documented; minutes and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Match funds to the quote
steps.description: The specialist compares the amount and date received with the saved quote, checks the good-until date has not passed, that no new invoice or returned debit has changed the balance and that the difference is within the write-off tolerance.

error.defect_description: A shortfall above tolerance is accepted.

evidence.note: Overage and shortage handling at payoff is documented; shares and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a shortfall or overage
steps.description: The specialist calls or emails the customer or dealer to explain the difference, usually a payment after the good-until date, a debit that came out in the meantime or sales tax left off, and asks for the balance. Small shortfalls are written off within tolerance and overages are set up for refund after posting.

error.defect_description: Customer given a wrong balance, causing a second shortfall.

next.condition: within tolerance or overage to refund

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Post the payoff and terminate the contract
steps.description: The specialist recalls the saved quote in the payoff function, applies the funds from suspense, confirms the effective date and reason code (early buyout or trade-up) and posts. The lease system closes the schedule, stops future invoices and debits, reverses unearned income, records fees and sales tax and marks the asset sold; the amendment flows to billing.

error.defect_description: Wrong effective date or reason code, an asset left active or a debit not stopped.

evidence.note: Payoff posting steps follow lease system documentation; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Check for debits in flight and overpayments
steps.description: The specialist checks whether the next pre-authorised debit was already in the file sent to the bank before the payoff was posted, and whether the customer or dealer paid twice, and sets up a refund if so.

error.defect_description: A debit in flight is missed and the customer complains later.

evidence.note: Share with a debit drawn after the quote is an author estimate for a portfolio where about 85% pay by pre-authorised debit.

steps.name: Prepare a refund request
steps.description: The specialist completes the refund form with the amount, payee, bank details or cheque address, the lease system reference and evidence of the double payment, and sends it to the manager.

error.defect_description: Wrong payee or amount on the refund.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Approve the refund
steps.description: The lease administration manager checks the refund against the suspense balance and the payoff posting and approves it, or sends it back with a question.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Cash disbursement controls: refunds approved by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Refund cheques as one way to clear a payoff overage are documented; the approval step is an author estimate of a common control.

steps.name: Issue the refund in the payment run
steps.description: An accounts payable clerk keys the approved refund into the ledger's payables module and releases it in the next weekly EFT or cheque run through the bank portal.

error.defect_description: Refund keyed with the wrong bank details.

evidence.note: Weekly payment run is an author estimate.

steps.name: Second check of the payoff posting
steps.description: A second specialist compares the payoff transaction with the quote, the funds and the contract: all assets closed, billing and debits stopped, sales tax right and reason code correct, and signs the payoff checklist.

error.defect_description: A posting error passes the check.

control.basis: Maker-checker control over payoff postings tested by the external auditor and by conduit servicer reviews

next.condition: contract is in a securitised pool
contract funded on balance sheet or bank line

evidence.note: About 60% of contracts sit in conduit pools, consistent with the organisation file's 65% of receivables; the error rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Notify treasury of a securitised payout
steps.description: The specialist adds the contract number, payout amount and date to the daily pool change list in the shared spreadsheet and emails treasury, so the prepayment can be passed to the conduit and reported.

error.defect_description: Contract left off the list, found only at the monthly pool reconciliation.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreement: prepayments deposited for the conduit and reported in the monthly servicer report

evidence.note: Servicer obligations on prepayments are documented in an equipment lease securitisation; the spreadsheet list is an author estimate.

steps.name: Record pool removal and remit the prepayment
steps.description: A securitisation analyst updates the pool tracking spreadsheet, moves the payout amount from the operating account to the conduit's collection account through the bank portal and flags the contract for the monthly servicer report.

error.defect_description: Remittance amount differs from the pool balance.

control.basis: Conduit servicing agreement: collections deposited within two business days of receipt

evidence.note: The two-business-day deposit rule is stated in the cited securitisation; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Close insurance tracking
steps.description: The specialist marks the contract closed in the insurance tracking database so certificate chasing and any protection program fee stop, and notes that the customer's own insurer can be told once title passes.

error.defect_description: Protection program fee keeps billing after payout.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send the title transfer request
steps.description: The specialist creates a title transfer request in the lease system queue with the serial numbers, registration numbers and buyer, so the title team issues the bill of sale and discharges the personal property registration.

error.defect_description: Request not sent, so the customer or its bank chases a late discharge.

control.basis: Provincial PPSA duty to discharge a registration once obligations are performed (for example BC PPSA s.50(4): within 40 days after a written demand)

evidence.note: The discharge duty is stated in the BC Act; the request step and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the paid-in-full confirmation
steps.description: The specialist emails the customer a paid-in-full letter and, for a trade-up, confirms to the dealer that the old contract is closed so the new lease can fund.

error.defect_description: Letter not sent; customer calls service.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Post payoff entries to the general ledger
steps.description: The nightly interface from the lease system to the general ledger posts the payoff entries (receivable closed, unearned income reversed, gain or loss and fees, sales tax payable) and passes sales tax amounts to the tax team's data, without a person touching them.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Payoff postings and gain or loss reporting are documented; the nightly batch is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Dealer request without customer authorisation
exceptions.description: The dealer cannot be given the payout figure until the customer signs an authorisation.

exceptions.name: Valuation needed for a fair market value or mid-ticket contract
exceptions.description: Asset management must value the equipment before the quote can be calculated.

exceptions.name: Concession or high-value quote
exceptions.description: A dealer or customer asks for a discount, or the amount is above the specialist's limit; the manager approves or sends it back.

exceptions.name: Quote expired and requoted
exceptions.description: The customer pays late or wants a new date, so the quote is redone.

exceptions.name: Shortfall or overage
exceptions.description: Funds received do not match the quote; the specialist chases the balance or arranges a refund.

exceptions.name: Debit taken after the payout
exceptions.description: A scheduled debit was already in the bank file; the customer is refunded after approval.

exceptions.name: Posting error found at second check
exceptions.description: The checker finds a wrong date, tax or open asset and the payoff is reversed and reposted.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from request to quote expiry (unused quotes) or to payoff posted and title request sent
benchmarks.population: Payout requests at a Canadian small and mid-ticket equipment lessor, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author estimate: standard quotes go out the same day and complex ones in one to three business days; unused quotes close when they lapse, typically 10 to 15 calendar days after issue; completed payouts are paid within about a week of the quote and take one to two more weeks to identify funds, post, check and hand off. No published lessor cycle time was found.

benchmarks.unit: share of payout requests that end in a payout

evidence.note: Organisation file process note.

benchmarks.unit: business days from receipt to deposit for the securitisation

evidence.note: Stated in the prospectus.
Section 50(4).

pain_points.description: Most quotes are never used, but each one costs a lookup and often a specialist's calculation.

evidence.note: Organisation file's 40% conversion; author view.

pain_points.description: Payout funds arrive without a contract reference and sit in suspense until someone identifies them.

evidence.note: Suspense warnings in payoff processing; extent is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: A scheduled debit taken after the quote leads to an overpayment, a refund approval and a weekly payment run, and often a complaint.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Dealers need trade-up figures quickly to close a new deal, but complex quotes wait in the lease administration and valuation queues.

evidence.note: Trade-up figures and dealer quote requests are documented; the delay is an author view.

pain_points.description: Securitised payouts are passed to treasury on a spreadsheet list, so omissions surface only at the monthly pool reconciliation.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: Equipment financing: Lease contract conditions
sources.supports: A Canadian bank lessor: buyout quotes are given by the customer service centre; the buyout is based on the number of payments remaining plus the buyout option in the contract; customer service calculates trade-up figures when new equipment is leased.

sources.title: Equipment financing: End or cancellation of a lease
sources.supports: Leases are non-cancellable but can be replaced or upgraded with a new lease at any time; end-of-term options are purchase at fair market value or stated option, renewal, return or trade-up.

sources.title: Partner with National Bank (equipment finance dealers)
sources.supports: Dealers can request buyout quotes and view financing history through the lessor's dealer portal.

sources.title: LeasePak reference guide: Payoff Quote [U0213]
sources.supports: Lease system payoff quote function: payoff methods including net present value of remaining payments and residual, manual fair market value entry for some methods, outstanding payments and assessments, sales tax screen, fees, security deposit, a Good Until date and saving the quote for later payoff processing.

sources.title: LeasePak reference guide: Payoff [U0103]
sources.supports: Payoff processing recalls the saved quote, takes the amount received, effective date, sales tax, overage (gain, suspense or refund cheque) and shortage (loss, allowance or invoice) and posts the payoff; payoff reversal needs a reason code; suspense balances raise a warning.

sources.title: Oracle Financial Services Lending and Leasing: Payoff quotes (A.1.8)
sources.supports: Payoff quotes may be requested by a customer, dealer or insurance agent, dated for a current or future date, with a valid-up-to date and fields for early termination, disposition and quote fees.

sources.title: Charter Equipment Lease 1998-1 LLC prospectus (Form 424B1)
sources.supports: Equipment lease securitisation serviced from New York and Toronto: the servicer may accept full prepayment only at not less than the prepayment amount (present value of remaining lease payments as set in the lease); payments on the leases are deposited within two business days of receipt; collection activity begins by telephone at about ten days past due with a letter at about twenty days.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: The Act covers leases for a term of more than one year; section 50(4) requires a secured party to register a change statement discharging the registration not later than 40 days after a written demand once obligations are performed.

sources.title: Lease End Specialist (job posting)
sources.supports: A lease-end role quotes buyout amounts and extension payments, administers extensions, terminations and amendments and handles early termination requests.

sources.title: Wages: Financial customer service representative (NOC 64400)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $22.00, high $30.39 (2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Accounting and related clerks (NOC 14200)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.12, median $25.00, high $37.00 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Customer service produces about 55% of quotes (standard contracts) directly from the lease system, as NBC describes for its customers; the organisation file's process description gives the calculation to lease administration, which here handles the other 45% and all completed payouts.
About 38% of quotes are paid at first issue and 10% are requoted, so about 42% of requests end in a payout, close to the organisation file's 40%.
Unused quotes end when the customer lets the quote lapse; the case's elapsed time for them is the customer's decision time, not the full quote validity period.
About 60% of payouts are on contracts in conduit pools; the rest are on balance sheet or on the bank line.
Title transfer and PPSA or RDPRM discharge are a separate process (transfer-title-and-discharge); this workflow ends when the request is sent.
External steps carry no touch time; the customer's and dealer's effort sits inside the waits.

Organisation file issue: lease administration has 10 specialists for payouts (about 3 FTE here), end of term, title transfers for about 1,250 cases a month, restructures and assumptions. That looks thin for 55,000 contracts unless customer service carries the standard quotes, as assumed here.
No Canadian lessor publishes payout cycle times or conversion rates; those figures are author estimates.
